text:
alyssa: Heads up — I'm seeing a p99 CPU+latency spike in us-east-1a canary after merge #5128. A10 / L4. Kernel selector flipped to `l4_fallback_v2` for ~20% of requests. p50 fine but p99 +200ms. anyone seeing this?

matt: on it. which cluster? can you link graph?

alyssa: us-east-1a canary (a10-l4). graph: https://metrics.redwood/internal/d/abc123/canary?from=-10m to=now

perf-bot: Alert: p99 latency up 210ms (baseline 45ms -> 255ms) in us-east-1a between 2149987200 and 2149987480. Token cost stable.

jia: hmm kernel selector change landed in pr/5128? I remember a heuristics tweak to prefer `l4_compact` for short-seqs, but fallback path `l4_fallback_v2` had a recent microkernel switch.

samir: quick hypothesis: fallback kernel has a different KV cache admission pattern leading to higher eviction churn -> more KV cold misses -> latency tail. saw something similar in eu-west last year.

alyssa: i pulled a sample trace, top shows repeated KV miss + small write cycles and socket stalls. snippet:```
TRACE 2149987401: req=0x7f... path=l4_fallback_v2 kernel=compact_seq
kv: miss (keylen=48) -> fetch remote 2ms -> insert -> eviction_pressure 0.8
socket: tx_queue_depth spike -> 120 -> wait 3-5ms
end
```

matt: interesting, socket tx queue spike suggests NIC egress queueing. are these nodes seeing noisy neighbor network bursts? infra ping?

infra-oncall: confirmed some noisy VM in us-east-1a host-37 reported high egress ~1.2Gbps around that window. Hosting A10 pods too. I'm investigating live placement.

jia: if network egress is flapping, the fallback kernel's batching heuristic may be opening larger packet batches which amplify tx queueing. original `l4_compact` limited batch to 8 tokens, fallback allowed up to 32. that could be it.

samir: can we repro locally by forcing kselector -> l4_fallback_v2 and injecting small packet delay? i can run a microbench on A10 locally.

matt: do we want a canary rollback of the selector tweak (pr/5128) or limit batch size on fallback? which is faster to mitigate?

alyssa: preference: quick limit to fallback batch size to 8, then revert selector change if needed. safer than full rollback.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered: pr/5128-hotfix (limit l4_fallback_v2 batch_max=8) -> canary us-east-1a started at 2149987590.

perf-bot: Canary metrics (post-hotfix) show p99 back to 60ms within 2m. p99 delta -195ms.

samir: local repro with net-delay 2-5ms + forced fallback showed same p99 spike until batch_max reduced. root cause confirmed: batch sizing amplifies NIC queueing under egress contention.

matt: created follow-up issue #5994 to: (1) add adaptive batch cap by observed tx_queue_depth, (2) add kselector test that simulates NIC egress contention, (3) monitor KV eviction churn in canaries.

alyssa: thanks all. leaving canary on hotfix for now. adding rollout hold to PR 5128 until proper tests land. @infra-oncall can you keep an eye for noisy host placements and move problematic VMs?

infra-oncall: will do. moved host-37 off critical A10 pool at 2149987801.

matt: summary: regression introduced by selector change + fallback kernel batch limit exposing noisy egress -> p99 spike. mitigated with batch cap hotfix, follow-ups created. :thumbsup:
